clue.text: Shows about how old the trousers are

indicators.note: the trousers go about, i.e. surround, the words for how old

parts.note: pants is a word for trousers
how old someone is asks their age

explanation.surface: Someone wonders just how ancient a pair of trousers really is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AGE inside PANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageants are grand public spectacles or displays, a kind of show.

clue.text: Now getting into trim for the procession

indicators.note: one piece getting into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: to pare is to trim
AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, so it can stand for now

explanation.surface: A soldier is smartening up just in time for the march past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts AD inside PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a march or procession of people through the streets.

clue.text: Manoeuvre the doctor into the carriage

indicators.note: the doctor is put into the carriage, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: carriage in the sense of bearing or way of walking is gait
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic is bundled into a horse-drawn coach as a ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' means a coach in the surface but a person's bearing in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move or stratagem, a calculated manoeuvre.

clue.text: She has a pub back east

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a pub is read backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A woman owns a tavern out in the eastern part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns INN into NNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a woman's name, so it can stand for any female, a she.

clue.text: Flower in a pot?

parts.note: a flower that might be found in a teapot, since its name begins with the drink

explanation.definitionFit: The tea rose is a garden rose whose scent recalls tea, so it is literally a tea flower.

clue.text: The paper will come out at the end of August

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to issue is to come out, emerge

explanation.surface: A newspaper announces it will be published late in the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'August' is T; 'at' joins it to ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin, soft kind of paper.

clue.text: Not knowing or caring one has got into a mess

indicators.note: letters that have got into a mess are jumbled and need sorting out

explanation.surface: Someone neither aware nor concerned has landed in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: CARING and ONE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge, the state of being unaware.

clue.text: Makes a grab for the stolen picture

parts.note: snaps means grabs at quickly
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A thief snatches a stolen painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick photograph, an informal picture.

clue.text: Tree gnarled and strangely tiny forever

definitions.note: an adverb in the clue, while the answer is a noun as in for all time

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted, so the letters of the first word are twisted round
strangely signals that the letters of the next word come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An old twisted tree, oddly small, seems to have stood forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnarled' turns TREE into ETER and 'strangely' turns TINY into NITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, so for eternity means for all time.

clue.text: Foreigner it would be madness to give the run-around to

indicators.note: the run goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the word run taken from run-around
mania is madness

explanation.surface: A traveller from abroad would be mad to be messed about.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN goes round MANIA; Rumanian is an old spelling of Romanian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rumanian is a native of Romania, a foreigner to a British solver.

clue.text: It's foolish to include small bananas

indicators.note: one word is made to include another, holding it inside

parts.note: inane means foolish, silly

explanation.surface: It's silly to put tiny bananas in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, mad.

clue.text: A play by Shakespeare, she concludes

indicators.note: the answer is the part that concludes the play's title, its closing letters

parts.note: Macbeth is a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a Shakespeare drama by saying she finishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: The last four letters of MACBETH conclude the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is a woman's name, so it stands for a female, a she.

clue.text: Impress upon that you'll give a lift back to

explanation.surface: A driver insists on taking a passenger back.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to impress it on someone; to drive someone home is to give them a ride to their house.

clue.text: Having got on one's feet, had made one's way up

explanation.surface: Someone stood up and climbed higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen describes one who has stood up, and it is also the past participle of rise, to ascend.

clue.text: Pen a note for the doctor to look at

definitions.text: for the doctor to look at

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
E is a note in the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note for the physician to examine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is a pig enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an eye infection, the kind of complaint a doctor would examine.

clue.text: Conjectures about, as the balloon goes up

parts.note: taken as written
a balloon is round, like the letter O
rises means goes up

explanation.surface: Spectators speculate as the balloon lifts into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise about something is to speculate or conjecture on it.

clue.text: Prepared to accept charity

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to take help from others.
explanation.definitionFit: With one's hand out one is ready to receive something; a handout is a charitable gift.

clue.text: Going through with it if first given a drink

indicators.note: the single letter is given first, at the front of the charade

parts.note: per means through or by way of
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone will go through with it only if given a drink beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first given' puts A in front of PER, IT and IF.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Andrew is travelling about again — he likes to travel

indicators.note: Andrew is travelling, so his letters move about
about tells us the word for again is turned round

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Andrew is off on his journeys once more; he loves to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDREW is rearranged as WANDER and 'about' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer roams from place to place, someone fond of travelling.

clue.text: In practice, it is totally ineffective

definitions.text: In practice, it is totally ineffective

parts.words: In practice, it is totally ineffective
parts.note: a medical practice dispenses a dummy pill that has no active effect

explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medicine with no pharmacological effect.

clue.text: Eves Big Brother, in turn

annotationWithheld.why: Eves Big Brother, in turn (4): ORBS = eyes, and rev(BRO) gives ORB, but no clue word supplies the S; 'Big' gives nothing that fits, so the clue seems garbled as held

clue.text: You, she and he have finished with it

annotationWithheld.why: You, she and he have finished with it (4): THEE = you, but no parse of 'she and he have finished with it' builds THEE without a word doing two jobs; probably garbled as held
annotationWithheld.clue: You, she and he have finished with it

clue.text: The storm has wrenched a door half

parts.note: torn means wrenched apart

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A gale has ripped a door in two.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of DOOR is DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Agree to set the dog on the prisoner

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece set on another sits below it

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Warders consent to let a dog loose on an inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down answer puts CUR below CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to agree or be of the same opinion.

clue.text: Hard to cut the string

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
E is the name of a string on a violin or guitar

explanation.surface: It's difficult to snip through the twine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string' looks like twine but is a musical string named E.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe can mean harsh or hard, as in a severe winter.

clue.text: He's supported the addendum

explanation.surface: Someone is backed by an extra clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on a horse is borne up by it; a rider is also a clause added to a document.

clue.text: A nude girl enters, to music

indicators.note: the girl enters the other word, going inside it

parts.note: bare means nude
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An unclothed young woman walks in to a musical accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts CAROL inside BARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian boatman's song, or music in that rhythm.

clue.text: When put by, it's worth having

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
set means put or placed

explanation.surface: Money saved for later is well worth keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something valuable, a thing of worth to its owner.

clue.text: To beat the time by an hour, has to get moving

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
HR is the abbreviation for hour

indicators.note: the letters are made to get moving, shifting into a new order

explanation.surface: A racer aims to better the record by an hour and must hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get moving' rearranges HAS as ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to beat soundly, whether in a fight or a contest.

clue.text: Making a killing on a lot of land

parts.note: a mass is a large amount, a lot
an acre is a measure of land

explanation.surface: Someone profits handsomely from a big property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a killing' suggests profit, but the killing is slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the slaughter of many people, an indiscriminate killing.

clue.text: The remainder of, first return to the bush

indicators.note: first says the turned word comes before the other piece
return means the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: the rest is the remainder

explanation.surface: Someone tells the others to head back to the bush first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns OF into FO, which 'first' puts before REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Forest and bush both mean wild wooded country.

clue.text: Not stamped Out of work

explanation.surface: An unemployed person's letter goes unfranked.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-free mail needs no stamp; read literally, free of a post means without a job.
